pr_title: Suppress traceback when bad escape is used (#79364)
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
<!--- Describe the change below, including rationale and design decisions -->
This change fixes the issue generating traceback in the replace module, when an incorrect escape string is used.
The idea is simple: to wrap the code with try-except construction, checking for "bad escape" exception
Fixes #79364 
<!--- HINT: Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue -->

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below -->
replace

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
<!--- Include additional information to help people understand the change here -->
<!--- A step-by-step reproduction of the problem is helpful if there is no related issue -->
1. Create test yml file with content:
```
---
- name: Test replace module error
  hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: no

  tasks:
    - name: Test replace with bad escape
      replace:
        path: /dev/null
        after: ^
        before: $
        regexp: \.
        replace: '\D'
```

ansible-playbook replace.yml -vvv

The [documentation for `re.sub(pattern, repl, string, count=0, flags=0)`](https://docs.python.org/3.8/library/re.html#re.sub) states it will expand escape codes

> backslash escapes in it are processed. That is, `\n` is converted to a single newline character, `\r` is converted to a carriage return, and so forth. Unknown escapes of ASCII letters are reserved for future use and treated as errors.

However [documentation for the `ansible.bultin.replace.replace`](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/replace_module.html#parameter-replace) parameter only mentions backreferences

> The string to replace regexp matches.
> May contain backreferences that will get expanded with the regexp capture groups if the regexp matches.
> If not set, matches are removed entirely.
> Backreferences can be used ambiguously like `\1`, or explicitly like `\g<1>`.

It looks like there's been fixes to make the error message more presentable. Would it be better - instead - to pre-process the value of replace to escape backslash escapes except for backreferences? Otherwise users will have to pre-escape their escaping which may require many levels of escaping to pass through YAML and potentially also Jinja filters. Even if a fix only tackles the error message the documentation should be updated to inform users they are required to perform their own escaping.

Escaping the replace string within the module could be achieved with something like this.

```py
escape_re = re.compile(r'(?=\\[A-Z])(?!\\g<\d+>)', re.IGNORECASE)
result = re.subn(mre, re.sub(escape_re, '\\\\', params['replace']), section, 0)
```
